citations.quote:
Work in quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ over $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, with $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and the divided-power integral form $U_A$. For $j\ge0$ put $\ell_j=j+3$, $n_j=j(j+3)$ and $r_j=j+2=\ell_j-1$. Let $V(n_j)$ have divided basis $u_{j,k}=F^{(k)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le k\le n_j$, of weight $n_j-2k$. Let $d_j=\varphi(2\ell_j)/2$ and $p_j=q^{-d_j}\Phi_{2\ell_j}(q)$, where $\Phi_m$ is the monic cyclotomic polynomial. Define $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ and the $K$-linear operator

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^{t(\ell_j-1)}u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le j),$$

with $T_j=0$ on every other divided basis vector. Define $S=\sum_{j\ge0}T_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,k}=C u_{j,k}$.

Then $S^2=0$; $C$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$ have finite columns on the algebraic direct sum; and $B=\{b_{j,k}\}$ is a homogeneous $K$-basis. Its free $A$-span $M_A=C(\bigoplus_j V_A(n_j))$ is $U_A$-stable. The standard compatible bar fixes every $b_{j,k}$. The regular zero and infinity charts, and their crystal residues, are exactly those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus $(M,B)$ satisfies all four based-module axioms with integrability in place of finite-dimensionality, and its integral triple is balanced. No infinite vector or completed direct sum enters this construction. No choice assumption is needed.

For every $a\in U_A$, the raw-coordinate action is the finite-column operator

$$C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS.$$

In particular, with $G_j=\binom{n_{j+1}}{r_j}_q\ne0$,

$$E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=\frac{G_j}{p_j}b_{j+1,0}-\frac{G_j}{p_jp_{j+1}}b_{j+2,r_{j+1}},$$

and both displayed coefficients belong to $A$. This is a module-construction assertion; it does not assert a failure of tensor globalization.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

derivations.claim: Take the actual based chain of [F1] and the singleton seed $\{b_{0,0}\}$. Each vector of its field direct sum belongs to finitely many finite strings, so its $U$-orbit is finite dimensional. In particular $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,2}/p_0$ belongs to $V(0)\oplus V(4)$. The seed therefore has a finite field orbit, while the question asks for a submodule spanned by raw basis vectors.

For every $j\ge0$, write $G_j=\begin{bmatrix}n_{j+1}\\r_j\end{bmatrix}_q\ne0$. Since $b_{j,0}=u_{j,0}+u_{j+1,r_j}/p_j$, [F2] gives $E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=(G_j/p_j)u_{j+1,0}$. Furthermore $u_{j+1,0}=b_{j+1,0}-u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}/p_{j+1}$. The index $r_{j+1}=j+3$ is strictly between $0$ and $\ell_{j+2}=j+5$, so $T_{j+2}u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}=0$ and $u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}=b_{j+2,r_{j+1}}$. Thus the exact raw expansion is $E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=(G_j/p_j)b_{j+1,0}-(G_j/(p_jp_{j+1}))b_{j+2,r_{j+1}}$. The two displayed raw vectors are distinct, and the first coefficient is nonzero.

Let $W$ be any $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$ and containing $b_{0,0}$. If $b_{j,0}\in W$, its image under $E^{(r_j)}$ belongs to $W$ by $U$-stability, and the nonzero $b_{j+1,0}$ coordinate in step 1.2 forces $b_{j+1,0}\in W$ by [F3]. Starting from $j=0$, induction therefore gives $b_{j,0}\in W$ for every $j\ge0$. These are infinitely many distinct members of the field basis $B$, so $W$ is infinite dimensional.

Hence no finite-dimensional based subobject of $M$ contains the singleton seed $b_{0,0}$. The module satisfies all four actual based axioms and is integrable in finite Cartan type by [F1], so it refutes the stated universal finite-envelope assertion.

boundaries.reason: The refuted universal assertion is disproved by an explicitly nonempty singleton seed.
